Face à l'histoire est un podcast documen: Face à l'histoire is a documentary podcast launched in 2021 on France Inter by Philippe Collin. Each series dives into a major figure or period — the Dreyfus affair, General Leclerc, the deportees of 1945 — with a constant angle: looking at the past to shed light on the present.
Sa particularité tient en un mot : Phili: What makes it special fits in one word: Philippe Collin isn't a historian, he's a journalist. He doesn't recite a lesson, he leads an investigation. He questions the best specialists, puts the narratives in tension, and lets the archives speak. The result has crossed borders: 40 million downloads, and a full New York Times article in January 2026 devoted to this French podcast, in French.
Cinquante-cinq minutes par épisode, quat: Fifty-five minutes per episode, four to six hours for a full series. Careful sound design, rare archives, period voices, documentary editing — the format owns its length instead of apologising for it.
La méthode journalistique appliquée à l': Journalistic method applied to History. It doesn't feel like learning, it feels like discovering. The nuance is slight, but it makes all the difference.
La série sur les déportés ne vous enseig: The series on the deportees doesn't teach you a timeline: it makes you hear voices. Human history, with an emotional density that very few media reach.
C'est Lolo qui a insisté pour qu'on en p: Lolo insisted we talk about it, and his verdict is blunt: Face à l'histoire is right at the top. Not out of nostalgia or elitism — because this podcast teaches things you wouldn't have learned anywhere else, about Dreyfus, about Leclerc, about the mechanics of History with a capital H.
La limite est réelle, et Lolo la pose lu: The limit is real, and Lolo states it himself: it's not for everyone. Without a minimum of curiosity for the subject, you drop off before the end of a six-hour series. It's a podcast you have to earn. But those who commit never regret it — including Alex, who wasn't exactly volunteering to relisten to French history on a Sunday evening, and who comes away convinced: this podcast makes people who didn't like History want to take an interest in it.
